title: Fidelity topography: INT8/AWQ/GPTQ kernel landscape
content:
Purpose:
This doc records a purposely exploratory benchmark run that maps quality vs. latency/throughput across several quantization toolchains (INT8 static, AWQ, GPTQ-style post-training) and three in-house kernel families. Goal is to produce a compact set of heuristics we can apply in the routing layer: when to prefer a slower high-fidelity kernel vs. a faster lower-precision kernel for a particular request profile.

Summary of what we ran (high level):
- Models: LLaMA-2-13B, Redstone-7B (internal distilled release), and a trimmed 3B instruction-tuned model used for load tests.
- Quantization modes: per-channel static INT8 (calibrated with 20k tokens of representative text), AWQ 4-bit/8-bit hybrid profiles, and GPTQ 4-bit baseline (layerwise-greedy).
- Kernels: fast-gemm-v1 (vectorized GEMM with tiled memory layout), lane-tiler (memory-coalescing attentions), and fused-attn-lite (experimental fused attention + KV packing).
- Hardware: H100-80GB (primary), A100-40GB (secondary), and an older V100-16GB for stress/low-memory fallbacks. All runs pinned to a single GPU to measure per-device behavior.
- Workloads: short-chat (avg 40 tokens), long-context-probe (avg 1024 tokens), prefix-cache-heavy (repeated prompts to exercise KV reuse).

Metrics collected (per run):
- Latency percentiles: p50, p95, p99 (ms per request), per-token breakdown where applicable.
- Throughput: tokens/sec for steady-state generation (beam-free sampling, temperature=0.7).
- Memory: peak GPU memory (MiB) and working set after model load (MiB).
- Quality: delta-LL (change in mean log-likelihood w.r.t FP16 baseline on WikiText-103), LAMBADA completion accuracy, a 200-sample instruction-following checklist (pass@1), and qualitative hallucination notes for a small prompt set.

Key synthetic observations (most actionable/high-level):
1) Latency vs quality knee is strongly kernel-dependent. fast-gemm-v1 applied to INT8 delivered the best tokens/sec (up to 1.9x vs fused-attn-lite) but its delta-LL penalty on LLaMA-2-13B was consistently ~0.12 nats/token higher than lane-tiler+AWQ for long-context probes. In human terms: hallucination rate increased slightly on adversarial prompts where token choice matter.
2) AWQ hybrid profiles maintain quality much closer to GPTQ on short-chat but expose a throughput cliff on long-context when used with fused-attn-lite: the KV-packing assumption in fused-attn-lite prevents some AWQ micro-optimizations, creating a 20–30% p95 latency penalty vs same quant on lane-tiler.
3) GPTQ 4-bit (layerwise-greedy) often wins for the 3B trimmed model in quality vs throughput for constrained hardware (V100). On A100/H100 the speed gains are less impressive because vector-width and CUDA kernel layout favour INT8-optimized fast-gemm-v1.
4) Memory headroom and allocation patterns changed which kernels are feasible for a given payload. On H100, fused-attn-lite+AWQ could run with aggressive KV cache reuse and achieve lower p50 for long-context queries but at the cost of p99 spikes when background GC and kernel lane switching occurred.

Representative numbers (excerpt):
Model: LLaMA-2-13B, workload: long-context-probe (1k tokens), temperature=0.7, measured on H100
- FP16 + fused-attn-lite: p50=320ms, p95=790ms, p99=1.12s, tokens/sec=420, delta-LL=0 (baseline)
- INT8 + fast-gemm-v1: p50=185ms, p95=520ms, p99=820ms, tokens/sec=810, delta-LL=+0.18 nats/token, LAMBADA acc drop 3.6pp
- AWQ hybrid + lane-tiler: p50=240ms, p95=590ms, p99=940ms, tokens/sec=610, delta-LL=+0.06 nats/token, LAMBADA acc drop 0.8pp
- GPTQ-4bit + fused-attn-lite: p50=260ms, p95=600ms, p99=980ms, tokens/sec=580, delta-LL=+0.09 nats/token

Observed failure modes / oddities (field notes):
- Kernel lane thrash: when the scheduler switched between fast-gemm-v1 and fused-attn-lite for a multi-request batch (mixed model variants), we observed a 30–40% p99 spike for several hundred ms tied to kernel re-initialization and memory remapping. Implication: per-request routing must consider kernel affinity and try to steer requests with similar kernel requirements together.
- Calibration sensitivity: INT8 per-channel calibration using non-representative corpora (developer logs vs release prompts) produced a ~0.05 nats/token extra delta-LL for tails. Recommendation: enforce a workload-derived calibration step for customers considering static INT8.
- AWQ fragility with older drivers: AWQ microkernels depend on driver-level DMA patterns; older CUDA drivers on A100 produced subtle throughput regressions (~8–12%) vs H100 with latest drivers. Keep driver matrix in compatibility table.

Quick heuristics we can encode into routing logic (experimental):
- If request length < 64 tokens and model <=7B: prefer INT8+fast-gemm-v1 for cost-sensitive tiers.
- If request length >= 512 and involves LLM chains with intermediate caching: prefer AWQ+lane-tiler or FP16 fused-attn-lite for p99 stability.
- If request is labeled "safety-sensitive" or comes from enterprise tiers (SLA): pin to GPTQ or FP16 fused-attn-lite only.
- Avoid heterogeneous-kernel batches: co-locate requests by kernel requirement or drain one kernel pool before switching.

Next steps / experiments to run (priority list):
1) Micro-benchmark the kernel warmup cost: measure exact remap/reinit time when switching kernels under production allocator. We saw 120–240ms of overhead in traces that aligns with p99 spikes.
2) Generate a small param sweep for AWQ hyperparameters (chunk size, quant-center bias) to see if we can recover the 20–30% fused-attn-lite penalty for long contexts.
3) Test a kernel affinity scheduler prototype in our traffic-replay harness (use traffic pattern for paywall product) and measure service-level p99 change under 95th percentile load.
4) Add a small instruction-following eval to CI (50 prompts) to catch quality regressions <1pp beyond delta-LL measures.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is deliberately exploratory and mixes workloads; numbers are indicative rather than certified. Re-run with your workload slice if you want definitive picks.
- Attachments: raw CSVs and perf flamegraphs uploaded to the confluence page linked above.

Appendix (short):
- Sampling: all gen runs used the same tokenization and sampling seeds where applicable.
- Measurement tooling: combined trace from per-token hooks (runtime-inserted) and nvidia-smi snapshots; post-processed with our perf-parse scripts.
- Raw CSVs and perf artifacts: see linked Confluence page and attached GitHub PR for reproducible scripts.

End of note.
